summary: Small, well-factored loader module: per-platform path resolution, a cached name-keyed loader, and a path-based loader, plus two compile-time-literal/IR helpers. One genuine low-severity duplication: the per-platform CDLL-loading block (RTLD_GLOBAL on Linux/Darwin, winmode=0 on Windows, else raise) is copied verbatim in _load_lib_with_handle and load_lib_path. No dead code, no public/private discipline issues, no comment/code drift. Otherwise clean on the DES dimension.

findings.title: Duplicated per-platform CDLL-loading block in _load_lib_with_handle and load_lib_path
findings.claim: The platform-dispatch that actually constructs the CDLL handle (RTLD_GLOBAL mode on Darwin/Linux, winmode=0 on Windows, else raise unsupported-platform) is copy-pasted across _load_lib_with_handle (lines 159-164) and load_lib_path (lines 178-183). They are character-for-character identical except for the variable name (path). A future change to the load mode (e.g. adding a platform, changing RTLD flags, or fixing the Windows winmode) must be applied in two places; missing one silently desynchronizes the two loaders.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared block into a tiny private helper, e.g. `def _cdll_global(path): ...` returning the platform-correct CDLL handle, and call it from both _load_lib_with_handle and load_lib_path. Local, low-risk, removes the desync hazard. (The historical Windows c/m msvcrt fallback in _load_lib_with_handle stays where it is — it is name-keyed and does not belong in the path-based loader.)
